title: Phase 7 registers StableStakerV2 with the global Pauser while V2 is still paused, so the permissionless Pauser.pause() reverts EnforcedPause for 3 transactions, and indefinitely if the run halts there. This contradicts story 084's 'breaker stays live all session'
story: story-084 (auto-complete, machine-approved). Its NatSpec L33-36 and the //stable-staker-v2-cutover:broadcast doc key (package.json L52) claim the breaker stays live for the whole Ledger session.
relatedLedger: L-04 46c053534c58 (sibling mechanism in Phase 1, proposed fixed); L-03 0711215fcc17
description: V2 is paused in Phase 3 (pauser OWNER) and stays paused through the migration. Phase 7 then runs, in this order: `v2.setPauser(PAUSER)` (L605), `Pauser.register(v2)` (L606), `antimatter.setPauser(PAUSER)` (L607), `Pauser.register(antimatter)` (L609), and only then `v2.unpause()` (L614). `Pauser.pause()` (lib/pauser/src/Pauser.sol L56-69) loops `IPausable(c).pause()` over every registrant with no try/catch. Once register(V2) lands, the loop reaches V2, whose pauser is now the Pauser, and OZ `_pause()` reverts `EnforcedPause()` because V2 is already paused. The whole global pause reverts. This is the registered-while-paused brick that story 084 fixed for V1 in Phase 1 by unregistering V1 before pausing it. The mirror rule for V2 is to unpause before registering, and it is not applied. The window is not forced: `unpause` is owner-or-pauser, and `register` only requires `pauser() == Pauser`. The script's preview simulation runs only at phase0, after-phase1 and after-phase8, and the Phase-8/verify sweep checks only the end state, so nothing in the repo detects the window.
impact: For 3 Ledger-signed transactions near the end of the session (register V2, Antimatter.setPauser, register Antimatter), every EYE-funded `Pauser.pause()` reverts and pauses none of the 26-27 protocol registrants, including the live strategies YS_DOLA/YS_USDC/YS_USDE. If the session halts inside the window (Ledger timeout, RPC error, operator interrupt), the permissionless circuit breaker stays dead until someone resumes. The runbook tells the operator to run `:preview` before resuming, but on that halted state preview reverts at phase0 with 'first failing registrant: <V2>', because the tolerance covers V1 only. The operator is left without a rehearsal and without a clear explanation, and an operator who follows story 084's guidance ('a halt is dangerous only between setPauser and unregister') may walk away. A broadcast-mode resume does converge through the unpause gate. No funds move by themselves; the harm is losing the emergency pause while it is dead.
evidence: Fork, block 25981150. `forge test --match-path test/audit-run33/CutoverAuditRun33.t.sol --match-test test_P7W_registeredWhilePausedWindow -vv --threads 1` PASS: GLOBAL_PAUSE|P7-after-V2.setPauser(Pauser)|SUCCEEDED; |P7-after-register(V2)|REVERTED|err=0xd93c0665 (EnforcedPause); same after Antimatter.setPauser and register(Antimatter); HALTED_P7|preview run()|globalPause(phase0): ... first failing registrant: 0x5582...8161 (V2); |P7-after-V2.unpause()|SUCCEEDED|registered=27; the real _phase8_wiringAssertions passes on the replicated end state (fork-logs/r33-test_P7W_registeredWhilePausedWindow.log). Control test_P7W_fixOrderingControl PASS: with unpause moved before register, the breaker is live after every step (fork-logs/r33-test_P7W_fixOrderingControl.log). test_P7W_haltedStateBroadcastResumeConverges PASS: a broadcast-mode resume heals. The call order was checked against the anvil broadcast receipts: txs #41 setPauser(V2), #42 register(V2), #43 setPauser(Antimatter), #44 register(Antimatter), #45 unpause() (fork-logs/anvil-broadcast-gas-budget.txt).
recommendation: In `_phase7_finalize`, move `if (!_doneV2Unpaused()) v2.unpause(); require(_doneV2Unpaused(), ...)` to immediately after `v2.setPauser(PAUSER)` and before `IPauserRegistry(PAUSER).register(address(v2))`, so V2 is never registered while paused. The finalized marker (`v2.pauser() == PAUSER`) is unchanged, and a resume from 'pauser handed back, still paused' still converges through the same gate. Extend `test/CutoverStableStakerV2Mainnet.fork.t.sol` with a per-transaction Pauser.pause() probe across Phase 7, like test_P7W_registeredWhilePausedWindow. Correct the NatSpec (L33-36, L76-80) and the :broadcast doc key so they name the one remaining forced window: the single tx between V1.setPauser(OWNER) and Pauser.unregister(V1).

title: The story-085 aggregate floor counts a staker's permissionless V1.userMigrate self-exit as V2 principal loss. A correct cutover then fails :verify with a false 'below pre-migration principal floor' alarm, the smoke preview is blocked, and a halted run can never be resumed
function: _assertPoolPostMigration / _aggregatePrincipalFloor (reached from VerifyStableStakerV2Cutover._verifyPhase6_migration and from every cutover Phase-6 resume leg)
story: story-085 (floor), story-086 (the verifier reuses the floor; its NatSpec L45-46 says self-exits via userMigrate 'never deposit into V2' and excludes them from the per-user check, but not from the floor). The story-086 review/auto-complete notes say 'the aggregate floor and straggler checks still bound each pool' when discussing partial log sets. None of the 085/086 tests covers a userMigrate self-exit during the Migrating window, and the floor misreads that designed exit path as a loss.
description: The floor is `v2Staked >= (P - v1Staked) * (MAX_BPS - bps) / MAX_BPS - n * WEI_SLACK`, where `P = V1.migrationInfo(token).principalSnapshot` is frozen at `initiateMigration`. `StableStakerV1.userMigrate` (L593) is permissionless and not pause-gated. From the moment `initiateMigration` lands, any V1 staker can take their snapshot credit to their own wallet. `batchMigrate` then skips them silently (StableStakerV1 L539: 'already self-migrated positions return 0 and are skipped'), and on chain the broadcast's local-pass user list still succeeds. The self-exited principal remains inside `P` and has left `v1Staked`, but V2 never receives it, so `P - v1Staked` overstates what was due to move by exactly that principal. The per-pool headroom at the fork block is about 0.24 DOLA, 0.236 USDC and 6.46 USDe. Any self-exit larger than that trips the floor even when every remaining staker was migrated within bound. In the broadcast, the local pass plans and asserts before the self-exit and passes. The self-exit lands between the `initiateMigration` and `migrate` txs (the `--slow` Ledger session puts at least one block between them), and the chain ends correct. The post-chain checks that re-read live state then fail.
impact: (1) `:verify`, which `:broadcast` chains right after the address patch, reverts with 'cutover-post: V2 booked total below pre-migration principal floor (067)' on a correct cutover, and the chained `:preview` smoke test never runs. The operator sees a principal-loss alarm on mainnet with no loss, and may take unnecessary emergency action. (2) If the broadcast halted after that pool's migrate tx and before Phase 7 (for example the ETH shortfall in NEW-03, which halts at tx #37), every resume leg reverts at the same floor in its local pass. The resume cannot migrate the remaining pools or finalize without editing the script. V2 stays paused and unregistered from the Pauser, the V1 phUSD mint is not revoked, and V2 stakers have only emergencyWithdraw. No funds are lost, and the owner can recover with a script edit or manual transactions.
evidence: Fork, block 25981150, real phases, core and verifier. `forge test --match-path test/audit-run33/CutoverAuditRun33.t.sol --match-test test_SX_selfExitBetweenTxs_verifierFalseFailsOnFloor -vv --threads 1` PASS: SELF_EXIT|user=0x25AdA296...4eb1|V1principal=5499869851883238089|paidToWallet=5499860523851791803; all 29 other positions migrated; real Phase 8 passes; floor 1222483056933011776952 > v2Staked 1217223596276947632021; verifier revert 'cutover-post: V2 booked total below pre-migration principal floor (067)'; preview run() on the same state reverts identically (fork-logs/r33-test_SX_selfExitBetweenTxs_verifierFalseFailsOnFloor.log). Control test_SX_controlNoSelfExit_verifierPasses PASS with 29 users re-checked (fork-logs/r33-test_SX_controlNoSelfExit_verifierPasses.log). test_SX_haltedResumeCannotFinish PASS: halt after the DOLA migrate, then resume run() reverts on the DOLA floor; USDC poolState still Active, V2 paused and not registered (fork-logs/r33-test_SX_haltedResumeCannotFinish.log). The verifier harness is the story's own VerifyStableStakerV2CutoverHarness (injected addresses and recorded logs). Its live path was separately proven equivalent on anvil (fork-logs/anvil-verify-clean.log).
recommendation: Anchor the loss gate on quantities a self-exit cannot move. (a) Replace the P-anchored aggregate floor with an exit-realization bound read from V1: `(R, P) = V1.migrationInfo(token); require(min(R, P) * MAX_BPS >= P * (MAX_BPS - exitBps))`, where exitBps is 0-2 for ERC4626 and slippageToleranceBps + 1 for market strategies. That bounds the pre -> credit haircut for every user, however they exit. Keep the per-user credit -> credited check: in-leg in the cutover, and from MigratedOut/DepositedFor logs in the verifier. (b) Alternatively, keep the floor and subtract self-exited principal. In the verifier, sum the UserMigrated credits from the same log fetch and convert them back to principal (`credit * P / min(R,P)`, plus 1 wei per exiter). The cutover script cannot recover that from state, so (a) is preferable there. Add a StableStakerCutoverDust / verifier fork test where a staker calls userMigrate between initiate and migrate. Correct the story-086 review claim in the NatSpec.

title: The 46-transaction cutover fits OWNER's ETH balance only at the pinned 0.3 gwei, with 0.000147 ETH to spare. At 0.31 gwei or more, tx #37 (the USDe migrate) is rejected for funds and the run halts mid-Phase 6, and neither the script nor the runbook states an ETH budget
description: `:broadcast` pins `--legacy --with-gas-price 0.3gwei --gas-estimate-multiplier 200`, and its doc key says 'base fee was ~0.16 gwei at planning - re-check before signing'. Phase 0 checks owners, pausers, strategies and mint rights, but not whether OWNER can pay for the ~47 transactions. A full broadcast rehearsal on an anvil fork of 25981150 used 18,317,077 gas. OWNER's live balance is 0.005642012 ETH (nonce 1631, unchanged since run-32). At 0.3 gwei the run costs 0.005495 ETH and succeeds with 0.000147 ETH left. With the actual per-tx gas limits, a node's upfront `balance >= gasLimit * price` check rejects tx #37 (USDe `migrate`) at any price of 0.31 gwei or more, and tx #32 at 0.4 gwei. An operator who follows 're-check base fee' and raises the price even slightly halts the run mid-Phase 6.
impact: The halt lands after the USDe pool is initiated (V1 USDe funds idle, pool Migrating) and before its 7 stakers are migrated or V2 is finalized: V2 stays paused and unregistered, and the V1 mint is not revoked. The run is recoverable by topping up and resuming, since every step is state-gated, but it turns a single session into an unplanned halted state. Combined with NEW-02, the resume can be blocked. No direct fund loss.
evidence: fork-logs/anvil-broadcast-leg1.log: local anvil fork of 25981150, forge script --broadcast --skip-simulation --slow --legacy --with-gas-price 0.3gwei --gas-estimate-multiplier 200 --unlocked, ONCHAIN EXECUTION COMPLETE & SUCCESSFUL, 46 txs, OWNER balance after 146889306269851 wei. fork-logs/anvil-broadcast-gas-budget.txt: per-tx gasUsed; actual gas limits from `cast tx <hash> gas`; first rejected tx is #37 at 0.31-0.35 gwei and #32 at 0.4 gwei. The pre-tx balance before #37 was 1079992206269851 wei against a 3383096 * 0.3 gwei = 1014928800000000 wei requirement.
recommendation: Add a broadcast-mode pre-flight in Phase 0: `require(OWNER.balance >= CUTOVER_GAS_BUDGET * gasPrice * 12 / 10, "Phase0: OWNER ETH below cutover gas budget")`, with CUTOVER_GAS_BUDGET about 18.4M gas from the anvil rehearsal and gasPrice taken from `tx.gasprice` or an env cap. State the ETH budget in the :broadcast doc key (for example 'needs >= 0.0064 ETH at 0.35 gwei; top up OWNER before signing').

title: The package.json //StableStakerV2Cutover operator comment still describes the superseded story-082 end state ('2 bps + 2 wei', 'V1 pauser back to Pauser and V1 UNPAUSED'), the opposite of what story 083 made the script do
reconcilesTo: Q-02 1c859cdebb6424756c073b1358559f38d84feff33eb6f6a6563414e352a03542 (STILL-LIVE; same contract/function/rootCauseClass, so the fingerprint should reproduce)
description: L49 is unchanged at 29aeb2b. Besides the run-32 drift, it now also contradicts story 084: it says 'pause V1' in Phase 1, while the script runs the setPauser -> unregister -> pause retire triple, and it says 'V1 pauser back to Pauser and V1 UNPAUSED, ... a paused registered contract would make the global Pauser.pause() loop revert'. It contradicts story 085 by describing 'strategy principal >= V2 booked' as the post-condition, which is now a lockstep plus an aggregate floor. It does not mention the story-086 :verify step. Stories 084 and 086 both excluded it from scope.
impact: The primary operator summary of a 47-tx mainnet Ledger session describes the wrong V1 end state and the wrong safety checks. An operator who compares chain state against it would judge a correct cutover wrong, for example V1 left paused and unregistered.
evidence: package.json L49 at 29aeb2b, byte-identical to 884ccf8 (closure-manifest intentCommentDelta 'unchanged'); compare script L33-36, L315-348 and StableStakerCutoverCore L510-527.
recommendation: Rewrite `//StableStakerV2Cutover` to match 082 as amended by 083-086: Phase 1 V1 retirement (pauser OWNER, unregister, pause; V1 left paused), per-user bound 2/61 bps + 1000 wei, the aggregate floor plus lockstep, and the :broadcast chain `patch && :verify && :preview`. Or reduce it to a pointer to the script NatSpec and the per-variant doc keys.
